problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=4x-3y,\,y(-1)=1
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y\,(-\frac{1}{3}),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y\,(-\frac{1}{3})≈{{field-1}}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1),\,y(1)=1
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y(2),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y(2)≈{{field-1}}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=2,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=2-1=1.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{2}\,y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1) & =\frac{1}{2}y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3) \\ \frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}(1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})) & =\frac{1}{2}y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3)}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=1+1=2.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3)}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})} \\  & =\frac{1(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+3)}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)} \\  & =\frac{3}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)} \\  & ≈-7.77.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(2)≈-7.77.$
